Appendix B • Proofs & Comments

B.20 Partitions of unity, paracompactness and second countability (§8.2.1)

The integral (8.4) needs a partition of unity subordinate to the cover of \(\mathcal{M}\) by the chart domains of \(\mathcal{A}^\uparrow\) (Subsection 8.2.1). This appendix shows that partitions of unity subordinate to every open cover exist because \(\mathcal{M}\) is Hausdorff and second countable (Chapter 3), that the property they actually rest on is paracompactness, and that neither condition can be dropped. Compactness and closures are as in Appendix B.19.

  • Paracompactness. A refinement of an open cover \(\{ \mathcal{U}_a \}\) is an open cover \(\{ \mathcal{W}_b \}\) with every \(\mathcal{W}_b\) contained in some \(\mathcal{U}_a\). A space is paracompact if every open cover has a locally finite refinement: finitely many sets near each point, instead of finitely many sets altogether as for compactness. This is the property partitions of unity rest on. On the one hand, a partition of unity \(\{ \textrm{\runic ᚹ}_n \}\) subordinate to \(\{ \mathcal{U}_a \}\) contains one: the open sets \(\{ \textrm{\runic ᚹ}_n > 0 \}\) cover \(\mathcal{M}\), since \(\sum_n \textrm{\runic ᚹ}_n = 1\), each lies in \(\operatorname{supp} \textrm{\runic ᚹ}_n \subseteq \mathcal{U}_a\), and they are locally finite, as the supports are. Partitions of unity subordinate to every open cover thus exist only on paracompact spaces. On the other hand, they are built on a locally finite refinement, as below, where Hausdorff and second countability are what produce it.

  • Existence. Let \(\{ \mathcal{U}_a \}\) be an open cover of \(\mathcal{M}\).

    1. Exhaustion by compact sets (second countability). Every point has an open neighbourhood with compact closure: the preimage, in a chart, of a small open ball, whose closure lies in the preimage of the closed ball, compact, and closed since \(\mathcal{M}\) is Hausdorff. The elements of a countable basis of \(\mathcal{O}\) contained in such neighbourhoods still cover \(\mathcal{M}\) and have compact closures: call them \(\mathcal{B}_1, \mathcal{B}_2, \dots\). Set \(\mathcal{K}_1 \coloneqq \overline{\mathcal{B}_1}\) and \(\mathcal{K}_{j+1} \coloneqq \overline{\mathcal{B}_1} \cup \dots \cup \overline{\mathcal{B}_{m_j}}\), with \(m_j > j\) so large that \(\mathcal{B}_1, \dots, \mathcal{B}_{m_j}\) cover the compact \(\mathcal{K}_j\). Then every \(\mathcal{K}_j\) is compact, \(\mathcal{K}_j \subseteq \operatorname{int} \mathcal{K}_{j+1}\), and \(\bigcup_j \mathcal{K}_j = \mathcal{M}\).

    2. Compact rings. With \(\mathcal{K}_0 = \mathcal{K}_{-1} \coloneqq \emptyset\), the compact sets \(\mathcal{R}_j \coloneqq \mathcal{K}_{j+1} \setminus \operatorname{int} \mathcal{K}_j\) cover \(\mathcal{M}\), and each lies in the open set \(\mathcal{O}_j \coloneqq \operatorname{int} \mathcal{K}_{j+2} \setminus \mathcal{K}_{j-1}\).

    3. Finitely many bump functions per ring (compactness). For each \(p \in \mathcal{R}_j\), take a bump function \(\varphi_p \in C^\infty(\mathcal{M})\), \(\varphi_p \geq 0\), \(\varphi_p(p) > 0\), with \(\operatorname{supp} \varphi_p\) compact and contained in \(\mathcal{O}_j \cap \mathcal{U}_a\) for some \(a\) (Section 4.2; its extension by zero outside a chart domain uses again that compact sets are closed). The open sets \(\{ \varphi_p > 0 \}\) cover the compact \(\mathcal{R}_j\), so finitely many suffice. Over all \(j\), this gives countably many \(\varphi_1, \varphi_2, \dots\).

    4. Local finiteness (paracompactness). Every point lies in some \(\operatorname{int} \mathcal{K}_m\), which is disjoint from \(\mathcal{O}_j\) for \(j > m\), so it meets only the supports chosen for \(j \leq m\): finitely many. The sets \(\{ \varphi_n > 0 \}\) thus form a countable locally finite refinement of \(\{ \mathcal{U}_a \}\).

    5. Normalize. Near each point, \(\sum_k \varphi_k\) is a finite sum of smooth functions, hence smooth, and it is positive everywhere, since the sets \(\{ \varphi_k > 0 \}\) cover \(\mathcal{M}\). Hence \[ \textrm{\runic ᚹ}_n \coloneqq \frac{\varphi_n}{\sum_k \varphi_k} \] is a partition of unity subordinate to \(\{ \mathcal{U}_a \}\): \(0 \leq \textrm{\runic ᚹ}_n \leq 1\), \(\operatorname{supp} \textrm{\runic ᚹ}_n = \operatorname{supp} \varphi_n \subseteq \mathcal{U}_a\), locally finite by step 4, and \(\sum_n \textrm{\runic ᚹ}_n = 1\). \(\square\)

    Second countability enters in step 1, and only there: it supplies countably many sets, hence an exhaustion by countably many compact sets. Hausdorff enters in steps 1 and 3, by making compact sets closed. Compactness then reduces each ring to finitely many bump functions, and the rings, each meeting only its neighbours, make the whole family locally finite.

  • Hausdorff cannot be dropped. On the line with two origins (Chapter 3), take the cover by its two copies of \(\mathbb{R}\), \(\mathcal{U}_A \ni 0_A\) and \(\mathcal{U}_B \ni 0_B\), and group the functions of a subordinate partition of unity into \(\textrm{\runic ᚹ}_A\) and \(\textrm{\runic ᚹ}_B\), with supports in \(\mathcal{U}_A\) and \(\mathcal{U}_B\). Since \(0_A \notin \mathcal{U}_B\), \(\textrm{\runic ᚹ}_B = 0\) near \(0_A\), so \(\textrm{\runic ᚹ}_A = 1\) near \(0_A\), i.e. at all \(t \neq 0\) close to \(0\). Every neighbourhood of \(0_B\) contains such \(t\), so \(\textrm{\runic ᚹ}_A(0_B) = 1\) by continuity, contradicting \(0_B \notin \operatorname{supp} \textrm{\runic ᚹ}_A\).

  • Second countability cannot be dropped. A countable partition of unity subordinate to the cover by chart domains, as used in (8.4), forces it. Every point has some \(\textrm{\runic ᚹ}_n > 0\), so \(\mathcal{M} = \bigcup_n \operatorname{supp} \textrm{\runic ᚹ}_n\), and each \(\operatorname{supp} \textrm{\runic ᚹ}_n\) lies in a chart domain: countably many charts \((\mathcal{U}_k, \mathscr{X}_k)\) cover \(\mathcal{M}\). The preimages \(\mathscr{X}_k^{-1}\big( B \cap \mathscr{X}_k(\mathcal{U}_k) \big)\) of the open balls \(B\) with rational centres and radii then form a countable basis of \(\mathcal{O}\). The long line of Chapter 3, which is connected and cannot be covered by countably many charts, therefore admits no such partition of unity4, and integrals over it cannot be built from chart integrals as in (8.4).

4

Countability matters only for manifolds with uncountably many connected components, e.g. uncountably many disjoint copies of \(\mathbb{R}\): they are paracompact and admit partitions of unity, necessarily with uncountably many functions, and are not second countable.
